lesson.title: Calligraphy
lesson.title_ar: القسم الأدبي (8): فنّ الخط (الصيني والغربي والإسلامي) واشتقاق الصفات

lines: Para 1: The word 'calligraphy' comes from Greek . It means 'beautiful writing'. It is the art of fine handwriting and has been practised in many countries for centuries. In the Far East, a pointed brush is used. In Western and Islamic cultures, a pen is the calligrapher's tool.

Para 2: Calligraphy in China has a history going back thousands of years. There was a strong connection between painting and calligraphy because they used similar methods and materials. However, calligraphers were seen as scholars, while painters were seen as ordinary workers. It was not until the 5th century that they were treated as equals.

Para 3: In Western cultures, calligraphy was based on the Roman letters. Different styles were developed from these basic shapes. Calligraphers were often religious men and the most beautiful examples of Western calligraphy are usually found in religious books. The pages are made beautiful by the shapes of the letters, the pictures added as decorations, and by the right colours used.

Para 4: Calligraphy among the followers of Islam was seen as the greatest of the arts, because of the importance of the writing of the Holy Koran. Therefore, many calligraphers concentrated the name of God.

Para 5: As Islam spread, so did calligraphy. The art grew and developed and two main styles appeared. Kufic, an angular style for carving in stone, appeared in the 7th century. By the 10th century, Nashki, a more flowing style with rounded letters, appeared and Kufic had almost disappeared. New forms of calligraphy also appeared in art and architecture. Artists twisted words into circles, squares and other shapes, small enough to fit on a plane or large enough to decorate the wall of a mosque. Birds, fruit, animals and even the shapes of mosques, ships and the Islamic Star and Crescent became part of the calligrapher's art.

Para 6: A number of young artists today are interested in traditional calligraphy. A good example is a piece of modern calligraphy in the shape of the Hand of Fatimah. It was designed as a greeting card by the Lebanese artist Mouna Bassili Sehnaouri some years ago. It reads Ma sha' Allah - 'As God wills'.
Discussion: 1 Is calligraphy important today? 2 Should writing be easy to read or beautiful?

simple_explain.html:
• الخط الصيني: بالفرشاة المدبّبة، وكان الخطاطون يُعَدّون علماء (scholars) قبل المساواة بالرسامين في القرن الخامس.
  • الخط الغربي: بالقلم على الحروف اللاتينية (Roman letters) في المخطوطات الدينية المزخرفة بالألوان والصور.
  • الخط الإسلامي: أعظم الفنون لصلته بالقرآن الكريم؛ ظهر الكوفي الزاوي (Kufic, 7th c.) للنحت الحجري، ثم النسخ الانسيابي المستدير (Nashki, 10th c.) وتشكيلات المساجد والبطاقات الحديثة.

activities.prompt_literal: C These statements are true. How do you know from the text? Write reasons in your copybook.
activities.prompt_ar: استخرج الدليل النصّي لصدق العبارات الست في C الأولى (WB ص 93):

items.question: 1 Calligraphy can be produced in different ways.
items.model_answer: In the Far East a pointed brush is used, while in Western and Islamic cultures a pen is used; Kufic is carved in stone, and artists also twist words into shapes.
items.explain_ar: تنوع الأدوات والأساليب في الفقرتين 1 و5.

items.question: 2 Painters in ancient China used a pointed brush, like calligraphers in that country.
items.model_answer: The text states painting and calligraphy in China had a strong connection 'because they used similar methods and materials.'

items.question: 3 Painters and calligraphers are treated the same in modern China.
items.model_answer: 'It was not until the 5th century that they were treated as equals' (meaning since the 5th century they have been treated as equals).

items.question: 4 The Nashki style replaced the Kufic style.
items.model_answer: 'By the 10th century, Nashki, a more flowing style with rounded letters, appeared and Kufic had almost disappeared.'

items.question: 5 Early Islamic calligraphy did not include pictures of birds, etc.
items.model_answer: Para 4 shows early calligraphers concentrated on the Holy Koran and the name of God; Para 5 calls birds, fruit and animals 'New forms of calligraphy' that developed later.
items.explain_ar: بدايات التركز على القرآن الكريم ثم ظهور التشكيلات التصويرية لاحقاً.

items.question: 6 The art of traditional calligraphy has not died out.
items.model_answer: 'A number of young artists today are interested in traditional calligraphy' (for example Mouna Bassili Sehnaouri's greeting card).

hints: استشهد بالعبارات المباشرة من الفقرات 1 و2 و4 و5 و6.

questions.stem: In WB Arts 8 B, what does 'practised' mean in 'It is the art of fine handwriting and has been practised in many countries for centuries'?

options.text: b) done (carried out as a traditional art across countries)
a) done again and again to get better
options.why_wrong: معنى التدرب للتعلم لا يناسب القول إن الفن مُورِس في دول عديدة لقرون.
هذا الخيار ورد في سؤال الكلمة concentrated لا practised.
هذا خيار معنى كلمة so في العمود الثاني.

hints: قارن بين الممارسة الحضارية للفن على مدى قرون (done) وبين التمرين الشخصي.
questions.explain: المعنى في السياق هو ممارسة هذا الفن وتطبيقه عبر البلدان والقرون (done).

questions.stem: Which pair of adjectives from PB page 60 (WB Arts 8 C [D] table) comes from 'angle' and 'Lebanon'?

options.why_wrong: صيغتان غير موجودتين في الإنجليزية ولا في النص.
هما صفتان مشتقتان من point وWest.
rounded ليست في الجدول، وRoman مشتقة من Rome.

hints: وصف الكوفي بـ an angular style، ووُصفت الفنانة بـ Lebanese artist.
questions.explain: الصفة من angle هي angular (زاوي) ومن Lebanon هي Lebanese (لبناني).
